title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem IV asks for a continued fraction for the alternating series s = x/α − x²/(αβ) + x³/(αβγ) − … , where α, β, γ, … are arbitrary.

Solution (§46):
- Define the tails t = x/β − x²/(βγ) + … and u = x/γ − x²/(γδ) + … , and so on.
- Then s = (x/α)(1 − t), so x/s = α/(1−t) = α + αt/(1−t).
- Rewrite αt/(1−t) = α/(1/t − 1) = αx/(−x + x/t). This gives x/s = α + αx/(−x + x/t).
- The same identity holds for each tail: x/t = β + βx/(−x + x/u), and so on.
- Substituting repeatedly gives x/s = α + αx/(β − x + βx/(γ − x + γx/(δ − x + …))).

Theorem VIII (§47) states this result. It is the special case a = b = c = … = x of Theorem VII on the previous page.

§48 replaces x by x/y and clears denominators: x/s = αy + αxy/(βy − x + βxy/(γy − x + …)).

§49 takes α, β, γ, … = 1, 2, 3, … . The series is then 1 − e^{−x/y}, and x/(1 − e^{−x/y}) = y + xy/(2y − x + 2xy/(3y − x + 3xy/(4y − x + …))).

On the next page this is rewritten as x e^{x/y}/(e^{x/y} − 1) and specialised to x = 1, y = 1, 2, 3, … . For y = 1 this gives e/(e−1) = 1 + 1/(1 + 2/(2 + 3/(3 + …))).

In modern terms, this is Euler's transformation of a series whose successive term ratios are simple into an equivalent continued fraction, applied to the exponential series.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Each step checks: s = x(1−t)/α; αt/(1−t) = αx/(x/t − x); the y-scaling in §48 is consistent; and 1 − e^{−x/y} = x/y − x²/(2y²) + … is correct.

ideas.what: Converting an alternating series with term ratios x/α_k into an equivalent continued fraction, by expressing each tail through the next tail
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (equivalence of a series and a continued fraction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Introductio in analysin infinitorum, 1748, ch. 18; also E71)
ideas.where_published: Introductio vol. I ch. XVIII; E71 De fractionibus continuis dissertatio; also earlier sections of this paper E593

ideas.what: Continued fraction for x/(1 − e^{−x/y}), with its special case 1/(e−1) = 1/(1 + 2/(2 + 3/(3 + …)))
ideas.modern_name: Continued fraction for 1/(e^z − 1), equivalent to the exponential series
ideas.where_published: Euler's continued-fraction papers (e.g., E71, E123) contain e-related continued fractions; the series-equivalent form is standard in Perron's treatise

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine application of Euler's standard series-to-continued-fraction transformation, already in the Introductio. The exponential specialisation is classical and well documented.
